goal: The runner takes the next step. Each lane takes the first project under NEXT — `queue.md`'s order, then alphabetical, within its repository — whose plan on `origin/main` says `ready` and which no other lane holds, and either starts that step's session or writes the step `blocked` on `main`. Then the next one. There is no round that walks every project, no `skipped 28 (blocked 21, …)` line, and no project the runner tries and skips ten minutes apart for days.

A step the runner could not start is `blocked` on `main` with `blocked_by: { kind: "workarea", name: <reason> }` and a comment naming the path and the files, landed the way an archive is — a docs-only pull request the runner merges itself. The way back is `mc brief` or a planning session setting the step `ready` again; the runner never retries on its own. (Martin, 2026-09-08: "Om det var något som en LLM skulle kunna ta beslut som så skulle det ha gjorts vid första Runner-försöket. Då är det det som är fel. Rätt svar är inte en Runner-runda till.") Ruling 17 in `rulings.md`.

Two lanes in one repository take from the same ordered list and never the same project. The rule that split a repository's names by index — lane `k` of `n` takes every `n`th name from position `k` (`round()` in `src/mc/run.js`, `names.filter((_, index) => index % count === lane)`) — is gone. (Martin, 2026-09-08: "kodningen med jämna och ojämna rader för vilket projekt som tas ur är bota dumt skapat".)

Measured 2026-09-08 in `~/mc/runner/log/runner.log`: memoro lanes #1 and #2 each ended every round with `skipped 15 (blocked 15)` or `skipped 16 (blocked 16)` and `0 ran`; `sql-w3-email-closure` was merged, refused (`PLAN.json is not resolvable by the plan's rule — steps: 13 in the merge base, 13 on this branch, 12 on main`) and aborted every ten minutes since 2026-09-06T18:34Z; `sql-w1-universe-closure` has been `dirty worktree (.gitattributes, .github/workflows/deploy.yml, .gitignore +1039)` every round — a `git merge origin/main` a killed session left in progress (`MERGE_HEAD` present, unmerged paths) — and nothing on `main` says either project is stuck; `mc status` reads `~/mc/runner/unmergeable.json` to say so for one of them and `git status` for the other.
contract: A step is handed out only from the plan on `origin/main`, and `main`'s copy of `PLAN.json` is the one the runner obeys everywhere: in the order (`assembleQueue`), in the choice of step (`chooseKind`), and — new — in the workarea, where a `PLAN.json` merge the plan's own rule cannot resolve is settled by taking `main`'s copy. A step session still edits only its own step (`status`, `pr`, `comments`, `met`) and the runner still checks that on the way back in (`unauthorisedChanges`, `src/mc/plan-schema.js`).

The runner writes exactly one thing into a plan, and only on `main` through a docs-only pull request it merges itself (`landDocsPr`, the archive's door): the first not-done step's `status` to `blocked`, its `blocked_by` to `{ kind: "workarea", name }`, and one paragraph appended to that step's `comments`. Nothing else in the plan is touched, and the runner never writes `ready`. Setting a step `ready` again is `mc brief`'s or a planning session's, by hand, and stays so.

What blocks a step is a fact about the workarea or this machine that a person has to act on: a dirty worktree that is not a merge in progress, a worktree that could not be made, a branch that could not be moved or checked out, a merge of `origin/main` that could not be committed, a role or a tool that is missing, a held pull request that has had its one repair. What does **not** block is transient and not the project's fault: the STOP file, the quota pause, GitHub not answering `gh pr list`, a fetch that failed. On those the lane waits and asks the same NEXT again.

Two lanes never hold one project at the same time. The claim is in the process (`claims`, `src/mc/run.js`), taken before anything is touched and released when the step ends, whatever the lanes' count. `per_repo` and `total` (`~/.memoro/mc/lanes.json`, ruling 14) keep their meaning: how many lane loops a repository gets and how many steps this machine has in flight.

The page and the runner read one order. `nextSection` (`src/mc/page-collect.js`) already calls the runner's `assembleQueue` and `kindFor` so the two cannot disagree; whatever function the runner picks its next step with is the one the page draws NEXT from, and the lane blocks it draws are the lanes as they now are: the head of each is the project that lane starts next.

`~/mc/queue.md` stays Martin's *these first*: names, one per line. A name leaves it when its plan is `done` or has left `main`, and no longer the moment one step has run — with NEXT as the only order there is, a prioritised five-step project that dropped to alphabetical after its first step would be the old round again in another shape. `tidyQueue` still rewrites the file to that shape.

Nothing in this project stashes, resets or discards uncommitted work in a workarea. The one thing it removes is a merge of `origin/main` a session left in progress — `git merge --abort` returns the tree to the branch's own last commit, which is what the runner's own post-session abort already does (`run.js`, *the session left the merge of origin/main unfinished*).
out_of_scope: The gate, the merge lane and the merge queue (`repo-merge.js`, `merge-queue.js`, ruling 15): how a pull request lands is unchanged. So is `landProject`, `stackOrder`, `replayOnto` and `held.json`'s one-repair rule; what changes is only what happens *after* the repair is spent — the step is blocked on `main` rather than skipped for ever.

How `mc brief` and a planning session set a step `ready` again. Both already write plans under the rules in `docs/project/README.md` § *Who writes what*; the brief lists blocked steps (`blockedSteps`, `brief-collect.js`) and will list these with the rest. No new verb, no `mc unblock`.

The chores: the helper's collect, the intake drain, archiving done plans, closing finished workareas, the unreadable-plans file (`chores()` in `run.js`). They keep their own loop beside the lanes and are not touched, except that `tidyQueue`'s rule for when a name leaves `queue.md` changes as the contract says.

Any rebase. The runner merges `origin/main` into a workarea branch and never rebases it (`syncMain`), and the sweep that freshened every open pull request after a landing was removed on 2026-08-30 (`repo-freshen.js`, its header). There is nothing to remove here; this is written down because the round's merge-and-abort of a stuck project every ten minutes read like a sweep in the log, and it stops with this project.

The page's layout. NEXT, the RUNNER block and `mc status <name>` are re-fed from the plan on `main` and from the new picker; their shape is not redesigned. `blocked_by.kind: workarea` draws where a `decision` or `project` blocker draws, with the name as its reason.
`mc run --rounds N`. A round no longer exists, so the flag is retired with an exit-2 pointer (the form `mc-cut` gave a retired verb); `--once` stays and means one step.

success_criteria.check: `grep -c 'skipped [0-9]* (' ~/mc/runner/log/runner.log` counted before and after the runner restarted on the new code: the count stops growing. `grep 'next —' ~/mc/runner/log/runner.log | tail` shows the lanes' picks. Paste both in the PR.

success_criteria.check: A unit test in `tests/mc/run.test.js` drives two lane loops on one repository over a queue of three ready projects with a fake session that resolves on demand, and asserts the two never start the same name and that the second lane takes the *second* runnable name, not the second by index. Live: `awk '/step starting/ {print $2}' ~/mc/runner/log/runner.log` after the switch, checked against the session lengths on the `done rc=` lines.

success_criteria.check: Unit tests for each blocking reason in the contract assert the docs PR's content (the plan diff is exactly `status`, `blocked_by` and one appended comment on the first not-done step) and that a second pick over the same world returns the *next* name. success_criteria.criterion: `docs/technical/mc-run.md` describes the runner as it now is — a picker per lane, a blocked step on `main` as the one thing the runner writes into a plan, `queue.md`'s new rule — and `docs/project/README.md` § *Who writes what* names the runner's one write. `rulings.md` no longer carries ruling 17.

steps.title: Each lane takes the next step under NEXT, and the index split is gone
steps.done_when: A lane loop picks the first project in its repository's order that the plan on `origin/main` says is `ready`, that is not in flight, not held after its repair, and not claimed by another lane; runs it; and picks again. `round()`, `runLane`, `splitLanes`, the `index % count` split, `refusedLine` and `--rounds` are gone; `--once` is one step; `queue.md` keeps a name until its plan is done or off `main`; the page's NEXT reads the same picker; the suite is green.
instruction: Read `src/mc/run.js` from `round()` (about line 2087) up through `runLoop`'s `lane()` closure (about line 2290), and `runLane` and `planRefusal` above them, before touching anything. The shape today: `queue()` reads `queue.md`, every plan on `origin/main` and `gh pr list` once per repository; `round({ only, lane, count })` builds the repository's name list with `splitLanes`, slices it by `index % count === lane`, and `runLane` walks that slice in order calling `planRefusal` (the plan on main) and then `runStep` (the machine) per name, collecting refusals for one `refusedLine`. After a merged step the lane stays on its project for up to eight steps. `runLoop` runs `per_repo` such loops per repository plus `chores()` and `mergeLane()`.

Replace the walk with a pick. Write `nextFor({ repo, world, claimed })` — pure, in `src/mc/run-plan.js` beside `assembleQueue`, and exported — that returns the first name in `assembleQueue(queueText, plans)` order whose plan is in this repository, whose `kindFor` is not `skip:`, which is not in `claimed`, and whose open pull requests neither put it in flight (`inFlight`) nor hold it after a spent repair (`heldRepair` with `skip`). Return `{ name, kind }` or null. `kindFor` and `heldRepair` are already pure over the world `queue()` returns; `inFlight` needs `openPrsFor` from `project-prs.js`. This is the one function the page must share: make `nextSection` in `src/mc/page-collect.js` build its lane blocks from `nextFor` applied repeatedly over the same world with each pick added to `claimed` — the head of each lane block is what that lane starts next, and `lanesOf` goes if nothing else needs it. `machineState` stays the page's second reading per name, as it is now.

The lane loop in `runLoop` becomes: read the world for its repository (`queue({ only: repo.name })`), pick with `nextFor` against the process-wide `claims` set, and if there is nothing, log `<tag>: nothing to run — sleeping` once (not every loop — keep a flag so an idle lane writes one line, not one per idle sleep) and sleep `idleSleepMs`. If there is a pick, log `<tag>: next — <name> (step <i>/<n>)` and call `runStep`. `runStep`'s `claims` check stays as the last guard; the pick already respects it. Its answers: `ran` or `merged` → pick again at once (a merged project whose name is at the head of the order is picked again by the order, which is what *stay on the project* was for — delete the eight-step stay); a transient answer (`stop`, `skipped:prs-unknown`, `skipped:sync`, the bare `skipped` an UPDATE or a lost slot returns, and the quota pause which `runStep` already waits out) → wait `idleSleepMs` and pick again, without logging the same line twice in a row; any other refusal is step 3's business and until then is a skip like today, but it must not be picked again in the same pass — add it to a per-pass `passed` set so the lane moves to the next name rather than spinning on one, and clear `passed` when the world is re-read. STOP and UPDATE are read where they are read now: between picks. The drain on UPDATE (`draining`, `quiet()`) is unchanged.

The claim: `claims` in `run.js` is the set. It is taken in `runStep` today; the pick must see a claim from the moment a lane has chosen a name, so have `nextFor` take `claimed` as the set itself and add the name in the lane loop before `runStep` is awaited, and release it in `runStep`'s `finally` as now — one owner per name, whatever `per_repo` says. Two lanes on one repository read the world separately (two `gh pr list` calls, ten minutes apart at most); that is what the claim covers, and the open pull request covers the rest once the first session has pushed.

`--rounds` goes. In `src/mc/commands/run.js` the flag is parsed (`strictValues: ['--rounds', …]`, `num(scanned.flags.rounds, 0)`) and passed as `rounds`; remove it from usage and parsing, and answer `mc run --rounds N` with exit 2 and one line — *a round no longer exists; `mc run` takes the next step until STOP, `mc run --once` takes one* — the form `mc-cut` gave retired verbs. `runLoop({ rounds, once })` loses `rounds`; `--once` runs one pick over the whole queue (one lane, every repository, no chores, as now) and exits. The shared `round()` for a person watching is therefore gone too.

`queue.md`: delete `dropFromQueue` and its call after a step (`run.js`, *the queue is Martin's "these first", and it empties itself*). `strictQueue` in `run-plan.js` already drops a name whose plan is `done` or not on main; that is now the whole rule. Update the docstring on `assembleQueue` and `strictQueue`, and the header of `run.js` where it says *a name leaves it the moment its step has run*.

`refusedLine` and the `refused` collection go with `runLane`. What the plans refuse is on the page (`nextSection.skipped`) and was never read in the log. The per-name lines `runStep` writes for a machine refusal (dirty worktree, in flight, held) stay as they are until step 3 changes what happens on them.

Tests, in `tests/mc/run.test.js` (3 322 lines — read its helpers first: `makeRunner`, the fake `git`/`gh`/`session`, and how a world is built): `nextFor` tested on its own in `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` — order from `queue.md` then alphabetical, a claimed name skipped, an in-flight name skipped, a held-after-repair name skipped, a blocked plan skipped, one repository at a time. The lane test success criterion 2 names: two lane loops on one repository, three ready projects, a fake session that resolves when the test says; assert the second lane starts the second runnable name while the first is in session, and that no name is started twice. Every existing test that drives `round()` or `runLane` is rewritten to drive the lane loop or `nextFor`; the ones that assert `refusedLine`'s text are deleted with it. `tests/mc/page.test.js`'s `nextSection` tests are kept and extended: with two lanes per repository the block shows two heads. `tests/mc/commands/run.test.js` (if there is one; else `tests/mc/run-doc.test.js`) covers `--rounds`'s exit-2 line.

`docs/technical/mc-run.md` is step 4's, but the docstrings you delete or replace in `run.js` are this step's — the header comment (*One round is one pass over the queue*), `round()`'s, `runLane`'s, `runLoop`'s lane comment. Write what the code now does and the date it changed; leave the history to the doc. Record the step in the plan the way a step session does: `status`, `pr`, the criteria met, and in `comments` what the code taught you — in particular whether anything besides `nextSection` and `runLane` read `splitLanes`.
comments: Nothing but `round()` and one test read `splitLanes` — the question the instruction asked. `nextSection` never called it; it had its own copy of the rule (`lanesOf`, grouping the runnable names by repository), which is why the two could have drifted the moment the runner's changed. `lanesOf` now applies `nextFor` repeatedly with each pick claimed, so there is one rule and the page's NEXT is the runner's own order. `docs/technical/mc-ui.md` still names `splitLanes` in prose — step 4's doc sweep.

One rule is here that the instruction did not name, and step 3 and 4 should know it exists: `pass({ last })`. *Pick again at once* after `ran` or `merged` is a spin when the step changed nothing — a session that opens no pull request and leaves its plan on `main` exactly as it found it would be restarted the second it ended, for ever, where the round's ten-minute sleep used to hide that at six attempts an hour. So the lane carries the `{ name, step }` it just ran, and `pass` skips that one name while the plan on `main` still shows the same step. A merged step *does* advance the plan, so a project whose next step is ready is still picked again at once, which is what the eight-step stay was for.

The picker now decides three of the refusals that `runStepClaimed` used to meet: `in-flight`, `held-after-repair` and `prs-unknown` (that last one is new to `nextFor` — without it, one repository's failed `gh pr list` ended `--once` for both). A lane therefore writes no runner.log line for them any more, which is the point: those were the lines written every ten minutes about a project nobody could act on. The words survive in `runStep` for the `RUN_REFUSALS` agreement table and in `machineState` for `mc status`, and the tests drive `runStep` directly to hold both. For step 3 this means the persistent refusals a lane can still reach are exactly `worktree`, `dirty`, `branch`, `sync`, `role-missing` and `tool-missing` — `in-flight` and `held-after-repair` never arrive there, so `blockStep` is wired to the six.

Criteria 1 and 2 stay `false` and criterion 6 with them: their live halves need a runner on this code, and the runner that ran this step is on the old code (it is what started this session). Step 3's instruction restarts it — take criterion 1's before-and-after `grep -c 'skipped [0-9]* ('` there, and criterion 2's `step starting` reading from the same log. The unit half of criterion 2 is in `tests/mc/run.test.js` (*two lanes on one repository take the next two runnable names, never the same one*): three ready projects with the second blocked, so the second lane demonstrably takes the second *runnable* name and not the second by index.

`docs/technical/mc-run.md` is step 4's and is untouched except for the flag list, which had a test pinning `--rounds 0 (the default) is forever` (`tests/mc/run-doc.test.js`); that paragraph now describes the flags as they are and carries a one-line marker saying the rest of the document is rewritten in step 4. `mc run start --rounds 3` gets the same exit-2 line as `mc run --rounds 3` because the answer lives in `parseLoopArgs`, which `start` also goes through.

For the tests: `runner.round()` is gone, and what replaced it in `tests/mc/run.test.js` is two helpers at the top — `lane(runner, repo)` drives `pass` until the lane would sleep, and `round(runner)` is `chores()` plus both lanes, which is what a round was. `pass` takes a `passed` seed for exactly that: a fixture plan never advances, so without it a lane would re-run the same project for ever in a test that has no clock.

steps.title: A `PLAN.json` conflict takes `main`'s copy, and a merge a killed session left is aborted
steps.done_when: In `syncMain`, a conflicted `PLAN.json` the plan's rule refuses is resolved by taking `origin/main`'s copy and the merge commits; a worktree with `MERGE_HEAD` present and no session on it has its merge aborted before the dirty check; `fromHead` in `planOf` and everything that existed for it — `markStuck`, `clearStuck`, `unmergeable.js`, its reader in `machineState` and the brief, and the `unmergeable` word in `RUN_REFUSALS` — is removed; the suite is green.
instruction: Read `syncMain`, `resolvePlanConflict` and `planOf` in `src/mc/run.js` (about lines 385–475), the `conflicts.some(isPlanPath)` branch in `runStepClaimed` (about lines 1655–1710) and `src/mc/plan-merge.js`. Today a `PLAN.json` conflict is tried by the plan's rule (`mergePlanText`: base, ours, theirs from the index); when the rule refuses — both sides edited one step, or the step count differs — the merge is left in progress, the plan is read from the branch's `HEAD`, that copy has no step to hand out, the merge is aborted, and the workarea is written to `~/mc/runner/unmergeable.json`. Every ten minutes, for days (`sql-w3-email-closure` since 2026-09-06T18:34Z).

Why `main`'s copy is safe to take. By the time `syncMain` runs, `inFlight` has already ended the pick on any open pull request of the project's, and `freshBranch` has already moved a branch whose content is in `origin/main`. So the branch's `PLAN.json` edits that are not on `main` are either work that landed in another form (a `Record PR N on step` commit whose PR merged, but whose squash `main` then re-planned over) or work no pull request carries — and `docs/project/README.md` § *Who writes what* says the plan the runner obeys is the one on `main`. Keep the rule as the first attempt — it costs nothing and its log line tells a reader what each side changed — and where it refuses, take `main`'s copy: `git checkout --theirs -- <path>` then `git add -- <path>`, and say `<name>: <path> — the plan's rule refused (<why>); main's copy taken`. `syncMain` then commits as it does when every conflict is resolved. `fromHead` in `planOf` has no case left: remove the option, the `git show HEAD:` read, and the `conflicts.some(isPlanPath)` branch in `runStepClaimed` with its `markStuck`. Ruling 10 in `rulings.md` was about this predicate; the code no longer has it, so this step's PR body says so and step 4 removes the ruling with ruling 17.

The killed merge. `sql-w1-universe-closure` on 2026-09-08: `git status` says *You have unmerged paths*, `MERGE_HEAD` is `72dd376…`, and HEAD is the branch's own `W1.12.6 — record the pull request on the step`. The runner's post-session abort (`run.js`, *the session left the merge of origin/main unfinished — merge aborted*) only runs in the round that started the session; a runner killed mid-session (rc 143, `mc run stop --force`) never reaches it. Before the dirty check in `runStepClaimed` (about line 1611): if `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` succeeds, `git merge --abort`, say `<name>: a merge of origin/main was left in progress — aborted`, and only then read `git status --porcelain`. An abort returns the tree to HEAD, which is the branch's own last commit; nothing a session committed is touched, and what it had not committed was already lost with the session. Do not abort on `REBASE_HEAD` or `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` — the runner never starts those, so one is a person's, and the dirty check reports it as it does today.

Remove `src/mc/unmergeable.js`, `tests/mc/unmergeable.test.js`, `markStuck`/`clearStuck` and `paths.unmergeable` in `run.js`, the `unmergeable` entry in `RUN_REFUSALS` (`run-plan.js`, with the comment that explains it), `unmergeableFor`/`describeUnmergeable` in `machineState` (`status-collect.js`) and the file's read in `brief-collect.js` (about line 1065, and the *Ready, and the runner cannot start it* section's use of it). The agreement test at the end of `tests/mc/run.test.js` asserts every `RUN_REFUSALS` word is answered by both `machineState` and `runStep`; it will tell you what else read the word. Delete the file on this machine at the end of the step and say so in the comments, or name it as stale if you could not.

Tests: in `tests/mc/run.test.js`, a workarea whose branch and `main` both edited step 3 of the plan starts a step with `main`'s plan text in the prompt and no `unmergeable` write; a workarea with `MERGE_HEAD` present and a clean index after the abort starts its step, and one that is still dirty after the abort is refused `dirty` (until step 3 blocks it). `tests/mc/plan-merge.test.js` is unchanged — the rule is still the first attempt. Then record the step in the plan as a step session does.
comments: `planOf`'s `fromHead` had exactly one caller-condition left (`conflicts.some(isPlanPath)`) and nothing else in the tree read `HEAD:` for a plan, so removing the option removed the last reader of a workarea's branch copy: the runner now reads a plan off disk and off `origin/main` and from nowhere else. The fixture's `git show HEAD:<path>` fake in `tests/mc/run.test.js` is kept on purpose — one test asserts HEAD is *not* read for a conflict outside the plan, and that assertion needs something to have been readable.

The predicate ruling 10 ruled on is therefore gone from the code entirely, not narrowed further: there is no `fromHead` to scope. Step 4 removes ruling 10 with ruling 17, as this step's instruction says.

One reader the instruction did not name: `status-project.js` read `unmergeable.json` too (`readUnmergeable`), because `mc status <name>` assembles `machineState`'s inputs itself rather than going through the brief. The `RUN_REFUSALS` agreement test would not have caught it — that test drives `machineState` directly — so a `grep -rn unmergeable src/` is what found it. `page-collect.js` and `page-cache.js` never read the file.

The MERGE_HEAD abort is unconditional and sits at the top of `runStepClaimed`, after the worktree exists and before `git status --porcelain`, so a lane that would have refused `dirty` on a killed session's leftovers now starts the step instead. The post-session abort is untouched, and `REBASE_HEAD`/`CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` are deliberately not aborted — the runner starts neither, so one of those is a person's work and the dirty check reports it as before.

One path can still stop a project on a plan conflict, and it has a test: git could not give `main`'s copy either — the three sides are not in the index, or `checkout --theirs`/`add` failed. Then the line says so (`the plan's rule refused (<why>) and main's copy could not be taken either`), the conflict is left, and the merge is aborted rather than left half-done. steps.title: A step the runner cannot start is `blocked` on `main`, and the runner never retries it
steps.done_when: `blocked_by.kind` accepts `workarea`; every persistent refusal in `runStepClaimed` ends with the first not-done step `blocked` on `origin/main` through a docs-only pull request the runner opens and lands, with a fixed-list name and one comment; `machineState` and `nextSection` read the block from the plan; the transient refusals wait instead; the suite is green and the live check in success criterion 3 is pasted in the PR.
instruction: The schema first, `src/mc/plan-schema.js`: `BLOCKER_KINDS` becomes `['decision', 'project', 'workarea']`. `validateBlocker` keeps `NAME_RE` for the name, so the names the runner writes are the fixed list below, all of which match it. `stale-blockers.js` reads only `kind: project` and must keep doing so — a `workarea` blocker is never stale by a machine's reckoning. Update the schema's docstring and `docs/project/README.md` § *The steps* where it lists the kinds (step 4 does the prose; the one-line list is this step's, so the schema and the doc do not disagree for a step's length).

The names, exported from `run-plan.js` as `WORKAREA_BLOCKS` beside `RUN_REFUSALS` so the page can spell them: `dirty-worktree` (uncommitted changes that are not a merge in progress — the comment names up to five files and the path), `worktree-missing` (`git worktree add` failed — the comment carries git's last line), `branch-unmovable` (`freshBranch` could not make `<name>-<n>`, or a repair's branch could not be checked out), `merge-uncommittable` (`syncMain` resolved every conflict and the commit refused), `role-missing` (`canon/roles/<kind>.md` absent), `tool-missing` (the launch adapter has no tool — the comment carries its hint), `held-after-repair` (the pull request `held.json` names has had its one repair and is still held — the comment carries the number and the hold's reason). These are the persistent words in `RUN_REFUSALS` (`worktree`, `dirty`, `held-after-repair`, `branch`, `sync` when it is the commit and not the fetch, `role-missing`, `tool-missing`) given names a person reads in a plan. What stays a refusal and never blocks: `stop`, `prs-unknown`, `sync` when the fetch failed, the quota pause, an UPDATE while waiting for a slot, `in-flight` (that is work, not a fault), and a hold at `repairs: 0` (that is a repair session owed, which the runner starts).

The write, `blockStep({ repo, name, reason, detail })` in `run.js`, shaped like `archiveDone`/`archiveIn` (about lines 1080–1180): a worktree of the repository at `~/mc/runner/block/<repo>` on a fresh branch from `origin/main` named `<name>-blocked-<stamp>` — with the project's name as its prefix on purpose, because `projectForBranch` (`project-prs.js`) then reads a block pull request that did not land as the project's own open pull request, and `inFlight` keeps the project out of every pick until it does land; nothing else has to know the branch exists. In that worktree read the plan with `readPlanText`, find the first step whose `status` is not `done`, and if it is already `blocked` do nothing (say so and return — the world was stale). Set `status: 'blocked'`, `blocked_by: { kind: 'workarea', name: reason }`, and append one paragraph to `comments`: `Blocked by mc run on <date>Z: <detail>. The workarea is <path>. mc brief or a planning session sets this step ready again once the workarea is fixed; the runner does not retry.` Write the file with the repository's JSON style (two-space indent, trailing newline — read how `archive-plan.js` or a step session writes it). Validate with `validatePlan` before committing — a plan the runner made unreadable is the failure `plan-intake.js` exists for, and it must not be this runner's. Commit `Block <name> step <i>: <reason>` with the detail as the body, push, `gh pr create` with the same title and body plus one line saying the way back, and land it through `landDocsPr` exactly as the archive does. Remove the worktree and branch in a `finally`. If the landing is refused, say so with the pull request's number and leave it open: `inFlight` covers the project from here, and the brief reads open pull requests.

Where it is called: every persistent refusal in `runStepClaimed` returns through `blockStep` instead of `refuse` — after `abandonMerge` where a merge is in progress, so the worktree is left clean. The picker in step 1 then never reaches the project again: `kindFor` reads the plan on `main` as `skip:blocked`. `machineState` (`status-collect.js`) loses the readings the block replaced — the dirty check and `held-after-repair` — only where the plan on `main` already says `blocked`; where the plan says `ready` and the worktree is dirty, it still says so (that is the window between the pick and the landed block, and the page must not read it as runnable). Keep the `RUN_REFUSALS` agreement test honest: every word still in the list is answered by both, and every `WORKAREA_BLOCKS` name has one test that drives it through `runStepClaimed` and asserts the pull request's title, the plan diff (`unauthorisedChanges`-shaped: only `steps[i].status`, `blocked_by`, and one new `comments` entry), and that the next pick over the re-read world returns the next name.

`nextSection` and the page: a `workarea` blocker is counted with the other blocked plans and drawn where a blocker is drawn, with `blocked_by.name` as the word. The brief's *Ready, and the runner cannot start it* section (`brief-collect.js`, about line 951) has no source left after step 2 removed `unmergeable.json`; its remaining sources (dirty worktrees the runner has not yet picked) are worth one line each still, but a `workarea` blocker must appear under the brief's blocked steps (`blockedSteps`) with its comment, because the brief is the way back — read `canon/roles/brief.md` to see how a blocked step is put to Martin, and make sure a `workarea` block reads as *fix the workarea, then set the step ready* rather than as a decision to take.

Live: restart the runner on this code (`mc run --update` after the PR lands, or `mc run stop` and `mc run start`), watch `~/mc/runner/log/runner.log` for `sql-w1-universe-closure` and `sql-w3-email-closure` — after step 2 both should start a session; if either is still refused, its block on `origin/main` is the proof instead — and paste the log lines and the `jq` from success criterion 3 in the PR. Then record the step in the plan as a step session does.
